annotatedSteps.description: Finding roots from factors (evaluated with ECF)
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
2x + 1 = 0 or x - 3 = 0
x = -1/2 or x = 3
So the roots are -1/2 and 3
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking:
2x - 1 = 0 or x - 3 = 0
x = 1/2 or x = 3
So the roots are 1/2 and 3

results.teacherNote: Marked against: Splitting the middle term correctly: 2x² − 6x − x + 3 = 0 (1); Factorising into linear factors: (2x − 1)(x − 3) = 0 (1); Finding the roots: x = 1/2 / x = 3 (1). Good attempt with clear presentation. Be very careful with signs when factoring out a negative common factor: −x + 3 must be factored as −1(x − 3), giving the roots 1/2 and 3.

summary: You demonstrated a clear understanding of the factorisation method and properly split the middle term. Take extra care with signs when grouping terms to avoid carrying errors into your final roots.
